findings: Scarcity responds strongly and monotonically to realistic supply changes near the league replacement boundary.
KDEF is deeper but remains materially binding after one or two additions; four useful additions reduce but do not eliminate its budget.
RUC scarcity is shallower and can be nearly removed by four plausible tall-forward additions, while one or two additions may be non-binding.
Removing one to four currently useful eligibilities increases scarcity sharply, as expected.
Cross-position effects occur because the 80 unrestricted scoring slots re-optimise, but the direction remains economically interpretable.
decision: Accept dynamic recomputation on each official position update. Do not freeze positional premiums or replacement lines across seasons. Position sensitivity is a feature of the market model, not instability, provided each published board records the exact eligibility snapshot and scarcity budgets used.
